Folks — quick technical notes from infra/implementation perspective. James, answering your bullets: 

1) Seed+delta support: yes. The attached "nimbus-mop-v1.xlsx" has a recommended schema for the seed export plus the incremental delta keys we need (updated_at ts, sku_id, content_blob). Our backfill job template supports a two-phase run: seed (full vectorization) -> incremental continuous ingest.

2) AtlasDB & KV prefetch: AtlasDB supports batched ANN lookups; we don't recommend an additional Redis layer unless you have 99th-percentile latency spikes in the vectorstore under normal load. Alternative: enable KV prefetch on the Redwood side and route hot keys to an in-memory cache within the serving runtime. Sergio, I'll sync with you on the prefetchtuning knobs.

3) Eval scope: 500 high-volume SKU queries is fine for smoke. We'll also provide an extended 5k eval set for a more comprehensive run. The smoke set should include: sku-edge cases, synonyms, and intent drift examples.

Operational gating checklist (short):
- Data export schema confirmed (owner: Nimbus)
- Seed job completes & vectors validated (owner: Redwood infra)
- Rerank smoke: baseline scoring vs current production (owner: Nimbus + Redwood analytics)
- Canary traffic shaping & failover policy defined (owner: Redwood SRE)

I'll attach the backfill workbook and a simple job template.

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
